A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ImitSAT research. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching despite added material and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original propagation and runtime comparisons, KeyTrace replay measurements, and query-timing, augmentation and curriculum experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds SATCOMP evaluation, retrained baselines, additional ablations, and CaDiCaL/Kissat integration results.

M1.justification: The main KeyTrace construction, Perceiver AR learner, behavior-cloning objective and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendices P and Q introduce experimental alternatives: a self-supervised GNN encoder replacing CNF tokens with variable embeddings, and Top-K legal-action selection instead of immediate heuristic fallback. These supplement the retained method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates planted random 3-SAT and five structured SATLIB families. Appendix M adds a distinct competition-derived, industrial-style SATCOMP domain. This materially broadens evaluation coverage, although the subset remains restricted to at most 100 variables and formulas fitting the model context.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add GQSAT* and SATformer* trained on the authors' data, plus explicit KeyTrace comparator rows. KeyTrace previously appeared only in the replay analysis. Appendix O adds MiniSAT to a direct runtime comparison, while Appendix R compares ImitSAT integrations against CaDiCaL and Kissat baselines. The original learned comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include matched-training controls, expanded query budgets and schedules, a 10-second MiniSAT cap and 30-instance runtime groups for SATCOMP, and runtime comparisons on the 50 hardest instances per range. CaDiCaL evaluation excludes preprocessing-solved instances; Kissat also receives a probing-disabled condition, with propagation normalized to the respective host solver. Figure 4 additionally changes PRET from four to five plotted instances.

E4.justification: The original augmentation, curriculum and single-query timing analyses remain. Appendix E adds delayed versus distributed versus immediate three-call schedules on the 100-variable and AIM sets. New analyses examine budget saturation, GNN input substitution, Top-K masking versus fallback, and how Kissat preprocessing affects opportunities for learned branching.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. v2 continues point-estimate reporting; its SATCOMP batch means aggregate instances rather than quantify repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Shared rows in Tables 1–2 and the retained ablations preserve their values, but v2 adds extensive comparator, SATCOMP, variant and modern-solver results. Table 12 newly reports 6.11 seconds for ImitSAT versus 6.44 for MiniSAT on 50 hard 61–100-variable instances; Table 16 also shows worse-than-baseline JNH propagation ratios of 1.15 and 1.46. Figure 4 adds five-call curves and revises PRET timings alongside its changed plotted instance count, preventing a same-setting speedup interpretation.

T1.justification: The SAT definitions, KeyTrace extraction equations, autoregressive formulation, loss, metric formulas and mathematical example in Appendix H are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: imitation-based CDCL branching, compact expert KeyTraces, reduced propagation, favorable runtime and generalization beyond random 3-SAT. The additional experiments support or qualify these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of applicability and failure conditions. It discusses diminishing returns from additional queries, difficulty-dependent runtime benefits over MiniSAT, overhead and underperformance of naive GNN integration, and low confidence as a possible explanation for Top-K failures. Appendix R explains why Kissat preprocessing can solve instances before learned branching is invoked.

D1.justification: Appendix P specifies the GNN configuration source, positive and negative edge sampling, and embedding substitution procedure. Appendix R identifies the PySAT interface and solver configuration choices. These add reproducibility information for new experiments; the original architecture and hardware disclosures, code/model link and release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds He et al. (2014) and Khalil et al. (2016), explicitly distinguishing MIP branching from SAT CDCL in search dynamics and learning formulation. Additional references support SATCOMP, modern solvers, PySAT and GNN efficiency discussion. This is a focused expansion of the existing positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local changes include an expanded related-work paragraph, an experimental roadmap, rewriting Appendix E, and adding Appendices M–R. Author contact information, conference headers and acknowledgments are also added; the established narrative is not extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain expert and retrained-baseline blocks, and Figure 4 is redrawn with additional curves and revised axes, legends and caption. New Figures 6–7 and Tables 9 and 12–17 substantially expand the visual evidence. The former Tables 9–10 become Tables 10–11 without substantive content changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation through matched-training baselines, direct MiniSAT runtime comparisons, modern-solver integrations, and tests explaining design choices and failure conditions. These address important gaps in v1's evidence for practical usefulness and transfer. Limitations remain: industrial coverage is small-scale, uncertainty is unreported, and Section 5.3 retains a best-or-tied claim contradicted by the new PHOLE comparison (GQSAT*-5calls 0.77 versus ImitSAT-5calls 0.82). These issues temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial improvement in validation and understanding of applicability.
